Allergies:
No Known Allergies / Adverse Drug Reactions

Chief Complaint:
Syncope; Cough

History of Present Illness:
___ y/o male with ischemic cardiomyopathy (EF 35% on MRI ___ 
and mild AS who presents with syncope, hypotension, and cough x 
1 week.

The patient reports ongoing cough for the past one week. 
Described as nonproductive although has chest congestion. 
Reports blowing his nose constantly and on ___ developed 
significant epistaxis requiring cauterization and packing in the 
ED. Given one dose of keflex at the time. The following day the 
patient reports fever up to 100.9F at home. Two days prior to 
admission, he described going to bathroom followed by sudden 
collapse and injury of his R arm during micturition. He denied 
prodromal chest pain or palpitations or other sx and was alert 
right after the event. Denies LOC. 

One day prior to admission, he had seen his cardiologist who 
noted he was getting a bit frailer, and was a little bit more 
unsteady on his feet.  He  His blood pressure on that visit had 
been running on the lower side 90/60, pulse is 60. His 
cardiologist cut his lisinopril in half to 5mg daily, hoping his 
balance would improve.

On the night prior to admission, he went to the bathroom and 
again after micturition felt weak in the knees and was caught by 
his wife who brought to ED. His wife found him starting standing 
in the bathroom and as she spoke to him he did not respond. He 
states that he heard everything his was wife was saying. 

He was sent to ___ where he received Levaquin, and he 
was transferred to ___ for further care.

In the ED, initial 
- vitals were: 98.9 75 79/47 18 98% RA.
- Exam showed he was dry with JVP 5, vasodilated (extremities 
warm) with persistent cough with yellow/green sputum
- Labs were notable for WBC 6.9, Hgb 8.7, Hct 25.4, Plt 102, Na 
128, K 5.0, Creat 2.6, ProBNP was 1565, Lactate was 0.8. UA was 
negative. Blood cultures pending 
- Imaging showed ECG with LBBB. CT at OSH c/w multifocal PNA
- He received 2.5L IVF in ED, Vancomycin and Cefepime, levophed 
0.03-0.25mcg/kg/min for a MAP>60, Triple L IJ & 3 PIVs were 
placed. 

Vitals on transfer T 97.5 87 116/58 16 98% RA.

Currently the patient reports ongoing cough. Difficult to 
produce sputum, although endorses chest compression. Denies any 
shortness of breath, chills, abdominal pain, nausea, vomiting, 
or diarrhea. Denies dysuria or increased urinary frequency.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS:  
Cardiac review of systems is notable for absence of chest pain, 
dyspnea on exertion, paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, or orthopnea. 
Does have intermittent leg swelling, although denies any current 
swelling.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo M with ischemic cardiomyopathy (EF ___ From echo ___ 
and moderate AS who p/w one week of cough, hypotension, and 
pre-syncope with findings of patchy infiltrates on CT chest c/w 
multifocal PNA in septic shock.

ACTIVE ISSUES:
# Septic shock: Patient presented with one week of productive 
cough, shortness of breath, low grade fevers at home, and 
hypotension with SBPs in ___. CT scan from ___ with 
multiple opacifications consistent with pneumonia.  No 
leukocytosis, and Influenza swabs were negative. The patient was 
admitted to the CCU and was started on norepinephrine for blood 
pressure support. He was resuscitated with fluids, and started 
on community-acquired pneumonia coverage with 
ceftriaxone/azithromycin. Blood cultures and sputum cultures 
without growth. Norepinephrine was weaned, and the patient 
improved. He was transitioned to oral cefpodoxime and discharged 
to complete a 5-day course of azithromycin and 8-day course of 
cefpodoxime for CAP.  

# Presyncope/Weakness: Pt presented with reports of pre syncope 
and generalized weakness at home. Most likely consistent with 
hypotension from septic shock. Initially concern may relate to 
symptomatic aortic stenosis, although repeat TTE with only mild 
AS. Also with dropping H/H in the setting of recent significant 
epistaxis requiring cauterization. He was transfused 1U of PRBCs 
as described below, and his infection was treated. Pt was 
cleared by physical therapy and discharged home with walker on 
___.

# Acute Kidney Injury: Admission creatinine at 2.6 from baseline 
of 1.1 in ___. Etiology consistent with pre renal azotemia in 
the setting of hypotension and septic shock. No evidence of 
decompensated heart failure. Pt was resuscitated with IVF, and 
creatinine quickly improved to 1.1 prior to discharge. 
Lisinopril and furosemide were initially held on admission. Home 
furosemide dose was restarted prior to discharge, and pt should 
be restarted on lisinopril in follow-up. 

# Aortic stenosis: Pt with hx of moderate aortic stenosis with 
valve area of 1.0-1.2cm2 on echocardiogram from ___. Likely 
contributing to pre syncopal episodes as pt preload dependent 
with AS. Due to concern symptoms may also be secondary to 
symptomatic AS, a repeat transthoracic echocardiogram was 
performed to evaluate AS. TTE from ___ with mild AS 
(1.2-1.9cm2), although difficult to visualize. Based on these 
findings, AS thought to be a less likely contributor to 
presentation.

# Systolic Congestive Heart failure: EF in ___ was ___. 
Repeat TTE during hospitalization estimated EF at about 30%. 
Secondary to prior ischemia. On admission, patient was septic 
and on pressors. Appeared euvolemic and was resuscitated with 
IVF. Home furosemide, spironolactone, and lisinopril were held. 
Pt given half home dose of metoprolol. On discharge, still with 
no evidence of fluid overload. Furosemide and home metoprolol 
were restarted prior to discharge. Lisinopril and spironolactone 
were held given relative hypotension, and should be restarted as 
outpatient.
to symptomatic AS, a repeat transthoracic echocardiogram was 
performed to evaluate AS. TTE from ___ with mild AS 
(1.2-1.9cm2), although difficult to visualize. Based on these 
findings, AS thought to be a less likely contributor to 
presentation.

# Anemia: H/H dropped overnight on ___ from 9.2/27.0 -> 
8.1/23.6.  Pt had been recently seen in the ED for epistaxis 
requiring cauterization. No further epistaxis during 
hospitalization so less likely cause of acute drop. Pt noted to 
have hematuria likely in the setting of traumatic foley. No 
melena or BRBPR. Pt was transfused 1U of PRBCs with appropriate 
bump. For prior epistaxis, pt completed 5-day course of 
mupirocen ointment from ED visit and was given nasal spray for 
comfort.

# Hyponatremia: Hyponatremic to 128 on admission secondary to 
hypovolemic hyponatremia. With IVF resuscitation, this resolved.

CHRONIC ISSUES:
# Hyperlipidemia: Continued on home atorvastatin.

# H/o Gout: Not active during admission. On allopurinol ___ 
BID at home. Renally dosed to 100mg po daily during 
hospitalization given ___. Home dose was restarted on discharge. 


# Anxiety: Stable during admission. Initially venlafaxine dosing 
adjusted for renal function, and with improvement, pt continued 
on home dose of venlafaxine ER 37.5 mg TID.

# Benign prostatic hypertrophy: Continued on home terazosin.

***TRANSITIONAL ISSUES***
-Held home lisinopril 5mg po daily and spironolactone 25mg po 
daily on discharge due to soft blood pressures. Pt should have 
repeat blood pressure in follow-up and consider restarting 
lisinopril.
-Discharged home on azithromycin x 1 day and cefpodoxime x 3 
days to complete HCAP coverage
- Pt instructed to weigh himself daily
-Code: FULL
-Contact: Wife ___ ___

Discharge Diagnosis:
1. Pneumonia/septic shock
2. ___
3. Anemia
